answer: An agent marketplace requires each identity to lock $100 for 30 days before it can bid, with no bond reused across identities. The public bond ledger acts as a lantern: auditors can verify the locked funds. A ripple of 1,000 fake accounts therefore requires $100,000 tied up at once. The delta between one identity and a thousand is $99,900 in extra capital, making mass entry costly even when generating new keys is free.
